subject: pc prior of range and sigma in SPDE pcmatern

messages.author: 616d580ea96dab5b
messages.subject: pc prior of range and sigma in SPDE pcmatern
parts:
Dear all,

I am confused about pc priors in pcmatern SPDE model, for example, we have

prior.range = c (0.05, 0.01) , it's meaning the probability that the mean of the range is below than 0.05 is 1%?
prior.sigma = c (0.025, 0.01) , it's meaning the probability that the mean of sigma is large than 0.025 is 1%?

In SPDE model, inla_res$summary.hyper will give a posteriori estimate mean and CI(or quant) of range and sigma, 

for example, we have

                      mean         sd  0.025quant  0.5quant 0.975quant   mode
Range for s 0.3207  0.1454         0.1491     0.2843        0.6979 0.2279
Stdev for s  0.0227  0.0037         0.0163     0.0223        0.0309 0.0217

I want to know whether the parameter specified by pc.prior is related to the mean of the posterior estimate or related the CI(or quant) of the posterior estimate.

Thanks for any suggestions and help！

Dong

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] pc prior of range and sigma in SPDE pcmatern
parts:
Hi,

no, the "probability that the mean of the range is below" is not the
correct interpretation. It's "probability that the actual range is
below".

The parameter settings in prior.range and prior.sigma specify such
probablities for the prior distribution.
The summary.hyper output summarises the posterior distribution.
For example, if you have prior.range = c(0.05, 0.01), that means that
a priori, P(range <= 0.05) = 0.01.
In your posterior summary, we can see that a posteriori, P(range <=
0.1491) = 0.025.
The a priori mean (expectation) for the range isn't explicitly
specified, but is some function of the prior.range value/probability
pair.
The a posterior mean (expectation) for the range is given by the
"mean" column, so in your case 0.3207.

Finn
